question.questionText: They ______ anything all the morning.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank requires a verb tense that describes an action that has not been happening continuously from the past until now. The sentence 'They ______ anything all the morning.' suggests that the action (eating) has not been taking place throughout the morning. The correct tense to use here is the present perfect continuous negative form: 'haven't been eating.'

  • haven't been eaten (verb phrase (passive)): 'Haven't been eaten' is the passive voice, which means 'they have not been eaten (by someone else).' This does not make sense in this context, as 'they' refers to people, not food.
  • haven't been eating (verb phrase (present perfect continuous negative)): 'Haven't been eating' is the correct present perfect continuous negative form. It means 'they have not been eating (anything) all the morning.'
  • have been not eating (verb phrase (incorrect word order)): 'Have been not eating' is not the correct word order in English. The negative should come before 'been': 'haven't been eating.'
